title: Billing Terms and Arrears Table — Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscriptions
content:
# Billing Terms and Arrears Table

Accounts office table of the billing terms fixed for each tier of Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscriptions.

| Tier | Length of one subscription term (calendar months) | Subscription fee invoiced | Days from invoice date to due date (calendar days) | Late fee on an overdue invoice (percent per month) | Days past due after which reporting and dashboard access are suspended (calendar days) | Fee charged when a suspended or lapsed subscription is restarted (USD) | Days after the subscription year end within which a lapsed subscription restarts on the same baseline (calendar days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Utility Bill Tracking Subscription | 12 | annual | 30 | 1.5 | 45 | 95 | 30 |
| Metering & Dashboard Subscription | 12 | quarterly | 30 | 1.5 | 45 | 225 | 45 |
| Energy Analytics Subscription | 24 | quarterly | 30 | 1.5 | 45 | 350 | 60 |
| Fault Detection & Diagnostics Subscription | 24 | monthly | 30 | 1.25 | 30 | 550 | 60 |
| Measurement & Verification Program | 36 | monthly | 45 | 1.25 | 30 | 950 | 90 |
| Managed Energy Performance Program | 60 | monthly | 45 | 1.0 | 30 | 2200 | 120 |


## Table notes

- The term length is the length of one subscription term; the two guarantee tiers are written for 36 and 60 months.
- The billing frequency is how the subscription fee is invoiced: once a year on the Utility Bill Tracking Subscription, quarterly on the next two tiers, monthly from the Fault Detection & Diagnostics Subscription upward.
- Payment terms are calendar days from the invoice date to the due date.
- The late fee is a percentage of the overdue amount per month.
- The suspension figure is the number of calendar days past due after which reporting and dashboard access are suspended.
- The reinstatement fee is charged when a suspended or lapsed subscription is restarted.
- The restart window is the number of calendar days after the subscription year end within which a lapsed subscription may restart on the same baseline.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A Managed Energy Performance Program runs a 60 month term, is invoiced monthly on 45 day terms, carries a 1.0 percent per month late fee, is suspended 30 days past due, pays USD 2200 to restart, and may restart on its old baseline within 120 days of the year end.
